newsitem.title: PERU: Peru charges five workers in plane crash - papers.
newsitem.headline: Peru charges five workers in plane crash - papers.

text.p: A Peruvian state prosecutor has charged five Aeroperu workers with manslaughter in connection with the deaths of 70 people in the crash of an airliner in the Pacific .
The Boeing 757-200 plunged into the ocean off Lima last year, killing all its passengers and crew.
An official probe into the accident released in January showed it was caused by adhesive tape covering altitude and speed sensors, applied when the aircraft was painted.

The accused, who include the head of the quality control department and the paint workshop chief, shared responsibility for checking that the tape was removed after the aircraft was painted, said prosecutor Magda Atto Mendivil in the reports.

The taped sensors, used to measure atmospheric pressure, were found in the plane's main body on the sea floor where it crashed Oct. 2 soon after taking off from Lima's international airport for Santiago, Chile.
Atto said the plane's flight crew members were also negligent in not checking that the tape had been removed.
She also reserved the right to bring charges against air traffic controllers from the airport if the court case found that they bore some responsibility for the crash.
Aeroperu officials declined to confirm the reports.
judicial officials were unavailable for comment.

The tape caused the plane's computers "to go crazy" -- according to the Peruvian government -- and left pilot Eric Schreiber without instruments as he struggled to land the plane in thick fog for nearly half an hour. Friday, 18 April 1997 21:49:08 ENDS nN18211675
